content: Pellagra is a disease caused by a deficiency of niacin (vitamin B3) and protein, particularly proteins containing the essential amino acid tryptophan. Tryptophan can be converted into niacin in the body, so consuming foods rich in tryptophan, such as milk, can prevent pellagra even if niacin itself is absent in the diet. However, if dietary tryptophan is primarily used for protein synthesis, niacin deficiency may still occur. Tryptophan is an essential amino acid found in foods like meat, poultry, fish, and eggs. A diet that includes these foods reduces the need for niacin from other sources. The role of lysine in the development of pellagra remains unclear. Historically, native cultivators of corn in the New World used a preparation method called nixtamalization, which involved treating corn with lime (an alkali). This process made niacin nutritionally available and reduced the risk of pellagra. When corn cultivation spread globally, this preparation method was not widely adopted because its benefits were not understood. As a result, populations heavily reliant on untreated corn as a staple food began to suffer from pellagra. The disease was first described in Spain in 1735 by Gaspar Casal, who provided a clinical description in his posthumous work Natural and Medical History of the Asturian Principality in 1762. This led to the disease being referred to as Asturian leprosy. In northern Italy, where the disease was endemic, it was named pelle agra, meaning rough skin, by Francesco Frapoli of Milan. For centuries, it was believed that maize either contained a toxic substance or was a carrier of disease, as pellagra outbreaks were common in regions where maize was a dietary staple. However, the absence of pellagra in Mesoamerican populations, who processed maize using nixtamalization, eventually led to the understanding that the disease was caused by dietary deficiencies rather than toxins. In the early 20th century, pellagra reached epidemic levels in the American South. In 1915 alone, South Carolina reported 1,306 deaths from pellagra, and by 1916, approximately 100,000 Southerners were affected. At the time, the prevailing scientific belief was that pellagra was caused by a germ or an unknown toxin in corn. The Spartanburg Pellagra Hospital in South Carolina, established in 1914, was the first facility in the United States dedicated to researching the cause of pellagra. In 1915, Joseph Goldberger, assigned by the Surgeon General to study the disease, demonstrated that pellagra was linked to diet. He induced the disease in prisoners by controlling their diets and later showed that a balanced diet or small amounts of baker's yeast could prevent pellagra. Despite skepticism in the medical community, the link between niacin and pellagra was definitively established in 1937 when Conrad Elvehjem demonstrated that niacin cured pellagra in dogs. Subsequent studies by Tom Spies, Marion Blankenhorn, and Clark Cooper confirmed that niacin also cured pellagra in humans, earning them recognition as Time Magazine's Men of the Year in 1938 for their contributions to science. Pellagra is most common in populations that rely heavily on untreated maize as a primary food source, as maize is a poor source of both niacin and tryptophan. The disease is prevalent in rural areas of South America, parts of Africa, and historically in the poorer states of the U.S. South, such as Mississippi and Alabama. It was also observed among prisoners in Soviet labor camps (Gulags) and in individuals with chronic alcoholism. The disease is characterized by the four D's: diarrhea, dermatitis, dementia, and death. Other symptoms include high sensitivity to sunlight, aggression, red skin lesions, smooth and beefy red glossitis, insomnia, weakness, mental confusion, and eventually dementia. The treatment and prevention of pellagra involve dietary supplementation with niacin or foods rich in niacin and tryptophan. Alkali treatment of corn, as practiced in traditional nixtamalization, can correct niacin deficiency. A balanced diet that includes adequate protein sources is essential to prevent the disease.
